tasks.short: Visit schools for sensory-impairment tutoring and teacher consultation

steps.what: Read the pupil's existing support plan and sensory-access needs
Travel to the school and reach the agreed teaching space
Tutor the student with sensory impairments using appropriate accessible methods
Consult the classroom teacher about needs and agree practical teaching adjustments
Enter and check agreed adjustments in the existing pupil support records {OTHER}
Save the support-plan update in the same pupil record

tasks.design: Retain school travel, accessible tutoring and classroom-teacher consultation. Where agreed adjustments are already written in the pupil support records {OTHER}, configure only current-pupil and visit-date headings; the teacher still captures and checks the full meaning, then saves normally.
tasks.previous_blocker: Sensory-access needs are individual and must be tested with the student and classroom teacher.
tasks.enabler_now: Native record defaults can remove a small repeated heading entry without selecting teaching adjustments.
tasks.still_hard: A technique that appears accessible may fail in a noisy, visually crowded or unfamiliar classroom.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher reads the student's response and works with the classroom teacher on practical access.
tasks.altitude: A small reduction in repeat support-plan headings; tutoring, travel and educational judgement keep their time and responsibility.

reach.task: Review accessibility in a classroom activity
reach.learn: Sensory access and practical accommodation testing

evidence.claim: Native pupil-record defaults may remove repeat headings without changing sensory-access tutoring; this is a conditional model-knowledge design and not an observed school baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is a school visit already agreed through the existing service arrangement. Travel is retained; no recurring visit-scheduling baseline or termly office preparation is invented.

The pupil support plan comes from the responsible teaching team with authorised access. The visiting teacher observes actual response in s3 and agrees adjustments with the classroom teacher in s4. The first written update is fully represented in s5: it is the existing plan used by the classroom teacher between visits, not an added progress log.

Selected pupil ID and visit date come from the current record and agreed visit. Missing context and unclear adjustments are entered or clarified manually in retained s1/s5 time; no clean observation feed or diagnostic inference is assumed.

Only 0.9 of nine update hours is repeated pupil/visit headings. The remaining 8.1 covers first capture, individual wording, checking that the update expresses the agreement, and corrections. All live work and the one-hour ordinary author save remain. Test native defaults before code; no self-approval gate is added to saving.

No automatic sharing with another school, pupil assessment, formal support-plan adoption or parent send is claimed. If local practice needs a separate disclosure or approval, measure and retain that real action before extending this design; do not treat a save as a send.
unknowns: Whether the visiting teacher actually writes this existing shared support-plan update
Current form defaults and authorised school access
research_questions: Does the present support-plan update require any repeated heading entry beyond its substantive first writing?
Which adjustments need testing with the student before entering the plan?

already_counted.description: First capture and check the agreed support-plan adjustment

incremental.description: Check pupil/visit defaults after support-record form changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is 0.9 repeated-heading hours less 0.2 upkeep = 0.7. Cautious case: the school uses an unlinked bespoke plan or existing defaults already supply headings; retain all nine update hours and add no configuration, giving zero. Tutoring, travel, consultation and ordinary saving receive no cut.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The teacher continues school visits and direct sensory-access teaching. Any benefit is a small reduction in repeated headings on an actual existing support-plan update.
reach: Work with classroom teachers and instructional coordinators on practical sensory access
skills_to_grow: Test accessibility in the actual classroom
role.ambitious_version: A visiting specialist who gives students and classroom teachers practical accessible teaching support with clear existing plan updates.
